title: ELECTION RESULTS
full_story:
Illinois Governor JB Pritzker easily won reelection Tuesday night, defeating Republican challenger Darren Bailey.  He is the first three-term Democratic governor in the state’s history.  There are no term limits on governors in Illinois.

The AP has projected that Juliana Stratton will win the race for Dick Durbin’s Senate seat.  Representative Mike Bost won his 7th term for the 12th Congressional District defeating Democrat challenger and political newcomer, Julie Fortier.  Nikki Budzinski has been reelected to Illinois’ 13th Congressional District and Mary Miller has won reelection to the US House in Illinois’ 15th Congressional District.

In Clay County Voter overwhelmingly voted for Darren Bailey and Mike Bost both with 84% of the vote.  In County Board District K, Rachel Walker defeated David E. Johnson 191 to 80.  County Clerk and Recorder, Amy Britton, County Treasurer, Stacey Allen, and Clay County Sheriff, Andy Myers, all ran unopposed.

title: LAKE LAND RUNNER UP
full_story:
The Lake Land College Clay Target Shooting team was named the National Trap Shooting Champion Runner-Up Team at the USA College Clay Target Nationals.

The team placed second, trailing only Lindenwood University in the national event in which 244 athletes participated, representing 25 colleges and universities across the country.

“I am very proud of the way we closed out another fantastic season for our Clay Target team,” Clay Target Shooting Head Coach Josh Fulk said. “The team is still very young, with this being just our third year offering the sport at Lake Land.  Already, we’ve proven we belong alongside some of the most accomplished programs in the country.  I’m proud of the way our athletes performed and am looking forward to how this program continues to grow each year.”

Individually, Lake Land College Clay Target team member Collin Hewing of Mode, placed second in the High Gun Gold Male category, finishing with a score of 198/200.

The Lake Land Clay Target Shooting Team includes Freshman Ellie Hagen of Clay City.

title: FLORA STATE REPORT CARD
full_story:
State education officials have released the annual report card metrics for Flora CUSD 35, highlighting exceptional academic strides.

Student growth and achievement are significantly outpacing expectations.  In English Language Arts, Flora students achieved a massive 66.8% proficiency rate, comfortably beating the state average of 55.4%.  Math turnout was also strong, with the district hitting 42.3% math proficiency, which sits three points above the state norm.

While academics and a strong 81.2% high school graduation rate are keeping the district in the spotlight, administrators say they are continuing to manage tight resource gaps.  The state snapshot reveals Flora currently sits at a 72.6% percent of adequacy for funding.

Officials attribute part of this success to high campus engagement, noting an excellent 99% student participation rate on state assessments.

In other district metrics, Flora recorded a low chronic absenteeism rate of just 12.8% and reported a principal turnover count of one over the past cycle.

title: FF VET PARADE
full_story:
Everyone is invited to The Veterans Day Parade this Saturday, at 2 in downtown Fairfield.

Veterans and spouses are welcome to enjoy breakfast from 7 until 9 at the Catholic Church in Fairfield.  The Flag raising ceremony, National Anthem by Elizabeth Scarbough and a patriotic concert by The Roasted Chestnuts featuring Bruce Dickey on tuba begins at 1 in Freedom Park.  The parade line up will also begin at 1pm on North First Street in front of the Fairfield High Rise.

There is no need to register for parade entry, just show up and help honor our local veterans.  The 2026 Veterans Day Parade begins at 2 in downtown Fairfield.  Look for the WNOI Swag-N-Wagon, a new 2026 Jeep Wrangler Sahara with the military-inspired ’41 Olive Drab Green color.  It will feature our famous bubble blasts and our new 5ft tall “Stream in’ Eagle” riding on top.  WNOI will be handing out patriotic candy and our WNOI/Sherwin Williams Youth Sunglasses during the parade route.

All veterans, spouses & parade participants are also invited to the FNB Veterans Appreciation Meal at the Wayne County Senior Center following the parade at 245.  For more information, contact Clifford Reever at 516-3111.

title: EJ WATER GRANT
full_story:
Monday, Congresswoman Mary Miller announced $4.5 million in federal funding to support the expansion of EJ Water Cooperative’s Delbert Mundt Water Treatment Plant.  The investment will double the facility’s treatment capacity, strengthening access to reliable water service for families, farmers, and businesses across seven Central Illinois counties: Clay, Effingham, Montgomery, Fayette, Cumberland, Christian, and Shelby.

“Our farmers, small businesses, and rural communities are the backbone of America, and they deserve the infrastructure necessary to thrive.  I’m proud to have secured $4.5 million to support this critical expansion in Illinois’ 15th District,” said Congresswoman Mary Miller.  “This investment will meet growing demand and strengthen the essential infrastructure that families and businesses across our rural communities will depend on for generations.”

Founded in 1989, EJ Water Cooperative is the largest rural water cooperative in Illinois, serving a rural population of more than 48,000 residents.  The Delbert Mundt Water Treatment Plant was constructed in 2010 near Beecher City and serves EJ Water’s fastest-growing western service area.

As demand continues to increase, EJ Water has expanded its infrastructure to support rural communities, including the construction of a 250-million-gallon reservoir in 2023.  The cooperative also works with smaller municipalities facing aging or inadequate water treatment facilities, helping provide dependable, affordable water service to underserved communities throughout Central Illinois.

title: OLNEY FFA WINS AT NATIONALS
full_story:
It was a clean sweep for the Olney FFA at this year’s National Agronomy Career Development Event.  Competing against 148 individual contestants from 37 different states, Olney earned a gold ranking and secured the number-one spot in the United States.

The competition tested students on technical skills, including crop and weed identification, insect recognition, and general soil science.  Teams also had to work together on a problem-solving activity and defend their findings to a live panel of judges.

But Olney didn’t just walk away with the team trophy; they completely dominated the individual standings, taking home all four of the top individual spots in the nation.

Kaitlin Kocher led the country with a first-place finish.  Ezha Biyok secured second, Kylie Kocher took third, and Evelyn Volk completed the sweep by placing fourth overall.

The national championship team was coached by Olney FFA advisor Hayden Kinkade.

title: GATEWAY CHANGES DISINFECTANT
full_story:
Beginning Monday, November 16th Gateway Regional Water Company will begin a modified disinfection process using Free Chlorine instead of Chloramines for its predominant water disinfectant.  Beginning December 21st, they will switch back from Free Chlorine residual to the normal Chloramines residual for its predominant water disinfectant.

Customers with health issues should contact their physicians with any health-related questions.

Customers on Gateway Regional Water Company include the City of Flora; Clay County Water; Western Wayne Water Company; Village of Xenia; Village of Iuka; City of Kinmundy; Village of Alma; Village of Farina; Fayette Water Company; FMC Water Co.; NEMC Water Co.; Village of Patoka; Raccoon Water Co.; and Village of Vernon.

If you have any questions, please contact Gateway at 618-775-1004.

title: ISP NOVEMBER PATROLS
full_story:
Illinois State Police (ISP) Troop 9 Commander, Captain Bruce Waggoner, announced that the ISP will conduct Distracted Driving Enforcement Program patrols in Effingham and Wayne counties this month.  This program allows ISP to focus on distracted driving laws to prevent traffic deaths and serious injury crashes.

Distracted Driving is doing another activity that takes the driver’s attention away from driving.  Distractions can increase a driver’s risk of being in an accident.  According to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, over 3,000 people annually are killed in crashes involving distracted driving.  Reading a text message can take a driver’s eyes off the road for an average of five seconds and nearly 1 in every 10 injury crashes involved a distracted driver.

Officers will be on the lookout for drivers who disobey Illinois’ distracted driving laws.

This project is funded through the Illinois Department of Transportation.

title: CARLYLE LAKE CONSTRUCTION
full_story:
Waterfowl hunters visiting Carlyle Lake State Fish and Wildlife Area for the upcoming South Zone hunting season should be aware of ongoing construction projects that may affect site access and hunting conditions.

Flood gate rehabilitation and levee stabilization projects designed to protect the levee from erosion will delay flooding of moist soil units used for waterfowl hunting.  Construction equipment will remain on-site during the week and may affect hunters and other visitors.

To minimize disruptions, construction activities will be suspended during the youth waterfowl hunt November 7th and opening weekend November 14th and 15th.

Hunters are encouraged to plan accordingly, use caution near construction areas and follow all posted signs and access restrictions while visiting the site.

For more information, call the Carlyle Lake State Fish and Wildlife Area office at 618-425-3533 or email [email protected].
